answer: Grade each submission with five jurors and slash the outliers. Expire a juror's seat after one epoch; renewing it requires fresh work, so a panel cannot ossify. Block the assignment when two jurors share a subnet, a host, or a funding trail. A farm cannot wander between panels without leaving a trace on the knoll of assignment history, and the pool pulls auditors from a nebula of unrelated addresses. Divergence slashing plus expiry makes a captured panel cost more than the work it grades.
